t:
(a) The corporation shall be nonpolitical and, as an organization, shall not furnish financial aid or assistance to, or otherwise promote the candidacy of, any person seeking elective public office. No substantial part of the activities of the corporation shall involve carrying on propaganda, or otherwise attempting to influence legislation. 
    (b) 
The corporation shall have no power to issue any shares of capital stock, or to declare or pay any dividends. It shall also have no power to engage in any business activity for pecuniary profit unless the activity is substantially related to the carrying out of its objects and purposes, as set forth in section 2, or the raising of funds for the accomplishment of said purposes.
 
    (c) 
The property of the corporation is irrevocably dedicated to charitable purposes. Upon dissolution or final liquidation of the corporation, after discharge or satisfaction of all outstanding obligations and liabilities, its remaining assets, if any, shall be distributed in accordance with the determination of its board of governors, in compliance with its bylaws and all Federal and State laws applicable thereto: Provided, however, That its property shall not, in any event, inure to the benefit of any private person except a fund, foundation, association, or corporation operated exclusively for charitable purposes.
 
    (d) 
No part of the income or assets of the corporation shall inure to any member, governor, officer, or employee of the corporation or be distributable to any person during the life of the corporation or upon its dissolution or liquidation. Nothing in this subsection, however, shall be construed to prevent the payment of reasonable compensation for services rendered to officers and employees of the corporation and other persons, or to prevent their reimbursement for actual necessary expenses in amounts approved by the corporation’s board of governors.
 
    (e) 
The corporation shall not make loans to its members, officers, governors, or employees.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that the references to influencing legislation, elective office, and a board of governors signal outside involvement in government decisions. In fact the section only restricts a chartered corporation's own conduct: no political activity, no stock or dividends, charitable dedication of assets, no private inurement, and no loans to insiders. The board of governors decides the corporation's internal affairs, not any federal decision. Nothing requires or permits a federal actor to consult, hear from, or be sued by an outside party.
fable.s: No substantial part of the activities of the corporation shall involve carrying on propaganda, or otherwise attempting to influence legislation.

qwen_block.w: This section outlines the internal governance, non-profit status, and political restrictions of a corporation. It does not require the federal government to consult with or coordinate with outside parties before making a decision. The 'board of governors' mentioned is an internal body of the corporation, not an advisory panel involving the public in federal decision-making.
qwen_block.s: The corporation shall be nonpolitical and, as an organization, shall not furnish financial aid or assistance to, or otherwise promote the candidacy of, any person seeking elective public office. No substantial part of the activities of the corporation shall involve carrying on propaganda, or otherwise attempting to influence legislation.

opus.w: This section only sets limits on a chartered corporation's own conduct and on how its assets are used and distributed. The board of governors decides about the corporation's private property, not a federal decision, and nothing requires the federal government to consult outsiders, hold hearings or comment periods, or allow anyone to sue. Mentioning a board making a 'determination' looks procedural, but nobody outside the government takes part in any federal decision.
opus.s: its remaining assets, if any, shall be distributed in accordance with the determination of its board of governors, in compliance with its bylaws and all Federal and State laws applicable thereto
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** The tempting reading is that the corporation's "board of governors" counts as a governing body that brings outsiders into decisions. That fails the definition. This is a congressionally chartered corporation, and the section only limits what the corporation itself can do: no political activity, no stock or dividends, no private benefit from its assets, no loans to insiders. The board decides how the corporation's own assets are distributed when it dissolves. That is a private decision, not a federal one, and no outside party is consulted on any federal action.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines the internal governance rules and legal restrictions for a specific corporation, such as prohibitions on political activity, dividends, and private inurement. It does not establish any mechanism for the federal government to consult with or coordinate with people outside the government (such as the public, states, or independent experts) before making a decision. The 'board of governors' mentioned is an internal governing body of the corporation, not an advisory panel involving outside parties for federal decision-making purposes.
qwen_chat.s: The corporation shall be nonpolitical and, as an organization, shall not furnish financial aid or assistance to, or otherwise promote the candidacy of, any person seeking elective public office.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "board of governors" constitutes an advisory body or committee involved in decision-making. However, the text describes the internal governance and legal restrictions of a specific corporation (likely a non-profit or government corporation), not a process for external public participation in federal decision-making. The board members are internal to the corporation, and the section focuses on prohibitions (no political activity, no dividends, no private inurement) rather than consultation with outside parties.
